implementation_notes: Coroutines carry the budget in the Job hierarchy: cancelling a parent cancels its children automatically (structured concurrency), and kotlinx.coroutines' withTimeout(remaining) cancels the current coroutine with TimeoutCancellationException when the budget expires. A hop converts the incoming deadline into a Duration, derives withTimeout from what is left (never a fresh constant) and lets every child coroutine inherit the cancellation; runInterruptible bridges cancellation into blocking JVM code as thread interruption, and withTimeoutOrNull is the variant for when a timeout is a normal outcome. The classic Future-plus-timeout combination is replaced by the coroutine scope.
pitfalls: withTimeout is cooperative: the documentation's own example shows withTimeout(1.seconds) { Thread.sleep(10_000) } taking ten seconds; blocking calls need runInterruptible or suspending APIs.
TimeoutCancellationException is a CancellationException, so it does not fail the parent scope by itself - catch it, or use withTimeoutOrNull when a timeout should surface as a value.
Values returned from a cancelled withTimeout are lost and resources opened inside must be closed in a non-cancellable finally (withContext(NonCancellable)).
Starting a fresh coroutineScope with a new full timeout at each hop re-creates the sum; carry the deadline instant and compute remaining time locally instead.
